issue.title: Add aria-label to the booking page duration badge
issue.body: Harness test (simple change). In apps/web/modules/bookings/components/event-meta/Duration.tsx, give the duration text an accessible label like "Duration: 30 minutes" (localized, English key in packages/i18n/locales/en/common.json) without changing the visible text. Include a unit test.

pm.summary: Small accessibility fix to the booking page duration display: add a localized "Duration: X minutes" accessible label and leave the visible text as it is. Ready for implementation with a unit test.
acceptance_criteria: Problem: on the public booking page, `EventDuration` (apps/web/modules/bookings/components/event-meta/Duration.tsx) shows short text such as "30m" or "1h 30m". Screen readers read this as an unclear abbreviation. This affects screen-reader users who book events.
For a single-duration event (no multipleDuration, not dynamic), the rendered duration element has aria-label "Duration: 30 minutes" for a 30-minute event, and its visible text is still "30m".

When the event has multiple durations but `hideDurationSelectorInBookingPage` is true, the rendered duration text has an aria-label for the selected duration (or the default length if none is selected), e.g. "Duration: 60 minutes" or "Duration: 1 hour", and its visible text does not change.

When the multiple-duration selector is shown, each duration option has an aria-label in the same format (e.g. "Duration: 15 minutes"), and its visible label (e.g. "15m") does not change. The existing data-testid, data-active and click-to-select behavior still work.

The label spells out units with correct pluralization: 1 minute gives "Duration: 1 minute", 90 minutes gives a label that includes both "1 hour" and "30 minutes", and 120 minutes gives "Duration: 2 hours".

The label text comes from i18n: a new English key exists in packages/i18n/locales/en/common.json (e.g. "Duration: {{duration}}"), and the label is not a hardcoded English string. No other locale files are required.
The visible layout is unchanged: the same text, classes and positions as before, with no extra visible characters.
`getDurationFormatted` keeps its current output, so BookFormAsModal, which also uses it, shows exactly what it shows today.

A new unit test inside apps/web/ (e.g. next to Duration.tsx or in apps/web/modules/bookings/components/) renders EventDuration. It checks the aria-label for at least the single-duration case and one hours case, and checks that the visible short text is unchanged. The test passes with the repo's existing test runner.
Out of scope: the visible duration format, other event-meta blocks (location, price, etc.), the BookFormAsModal duration, non-English translations, and any dependency or tooling changes.

research.summary: Research done: EventDuration renders bare text fragments, so a wrapper element plus a new i18n key is needed. The tests need their own translation mock. Next: write the plan.
patterns: Cause: Duration.tsx:93 and :101 return getDurationFormatted(...) inside a bare fragment (<>...</>), so no element can hold an aria-label. A non-layout-changing wrapper (e.g. a plain <span>) is needed there. In the selector branch (:121-131), the aria-label can go on the existing <li> (keep data-testId, data-active and onClick) or on the inner <div className="w-max">.

getDurationFormatted (Duration.tsx:14-38) uses the short keys minute_one_short/hour_one_short/multiple_duration_timeUnit_short. It is also imported by BookFormAsModal.tsx:12/68, so it must not change. Add a separate long-form helper (e.g. getDurationAriaLabel) in Duration.tsx.

en/common.json already has plural long-form keys: minute_one "{{count}} minute" / minute_other "{{count}} minutes" (lines 1805/1807), hour_one / hour_other (1808/1810), and "duration": "Duration" (920). Use t("minute", { count }) / t("hour", { count }) for the units, and add one new key such as "duration_aria_label": "Duration: {{duration}}" above the ADD_NEW_STRINGS_ABOVE_THIS_LINE marker at the end of the file.
EventDuration is rendered only by Details.tsx:146 inside EventMetaBlock (icon=clock, className items-center). The visible text and classes must not change.

Test project: vitest.workspace.ts project '@calcom/web/modules/views' (jsdom) includes apps/web/modules/**/*.{test,spec}.tsx, with setupFiles apps/web/modules/test-setup.ts. That setup globally mocks @calcom/lib/hooks/useLocale with t = identity and mocks @calcom/embed-core/embed-iframe (useIsEmbed vi.fn). afterEach calls vi.resetAllMocks.

Because the global t mock returns the raw key, the new test must provide its own vi.mock('@calcom/lib/hooks/useLocale') whose t interpolates {{count}}/{{duration}}/{{unit}} and picks _one/_other plural forms (and handles the nested $t(...) used by the short keys) so it can check 'Duration: 30 minutes' and the visible '30m'. Another option is a real i18next createInstance loaded with en/common.json (i18next 23.2.3 is an apps/web dependency).

The test also needs to mock @calcom/atoms/hooks/useIsPlatform (as in Booker.test.tsx:105) and @calcom/web/modules/apps/components/AllApps useShouldShowArrows (returning { ref: { current: null }, calculateScroll: vi.fn(), leftVisible: false, rightVisible: false }), because AllApps pulls in heavy dependencies.

Booker store: use render from @calcom/features/bookings/Booker/__tests__/test-utils with mockStore { selectedDuration, state } to cover the hidden-selector and selector cases (pattern from DatePicker.test.tsx).

Test file style: colocated *.test.tsx next to the component (e.g. apps/web/modules/bookings/components/DatePicker.test.tsx), using describe/test from vitest globals and @testing-library/react screen queries.
Commit style: only one merge commit is visible (Merge pull request #17 from lucasgrocha/ci/harness-orquestracao), so there is little commit history to infer conventions from.

Unresolved for plan: whether the aria-label goes on the <li> or on the inner <div> in selector mode, and whether to add role="img" or another role to the wrapper <span> so screen readers announce the aria-label of a non-interactive element.

design_need.summary: No design needed. This only adds a non-visible accessible label and reuses the existing duration display without changing the layout. Next step: write the implementation plan.
